summary: Pavel Trost was a linguist who earned his Ph.D. under Friedrich Karl Slotty at Charles University and studied at Masaryk and Palacký Universities. He held posts at the Moravian Library, Masaryk University, Palacký University, and Charles University.
Pavle Jevtić worked in Indology and philosophy. He earned a Ph.D. from SOAS University of London around 1923–1927 and was a disciple of Dimitrije Mitrinović.

Pavlo Grigorovič Ritter was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the University of Kharkiv under Dmitrij Nikolaevič Ovsjaniko-Kulikovskij and with Karl Friedrich Geldner, later becoming a professor at the University of Kharkiv in 1921.

Pawan Goyal works in linguistics and Indology. He earned an M.Tech. at IIT Madras and a Ph.D. at the Max Planck Institute, where he was later a postdoctoral researcher, and has been affiliated with IIT Kharagpur (attested 2018–2025).

Pe Maung Tin worked in Buddhist studies, linguistics, and Indology. Educated at Rangoon, Calcutta, and Oxford, he was Professor of Pali and Principal at the University of Rangoon, University of Adult Education principal, and Burma Historical Commission chairman.
Pedro Manuel Castro Sánchez is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at the University of Sunderland, where he studied under Peter Harvey.

Pedro Roca y López was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Juan Gelabert y Gordiola and earned a Dr.phil. at Complutense University of Madrid. He held posts as librarian at the University of Barcelona and at Spain's National Library.

id: P:Pedro Urbano González de la Calle
summary: Pedro Urbano González de la Calle was a linguist and Indologist who earned his Ph.D. at Complutense University under Mario Daza de Campos. He held professorships and posts in Salamanca, Valencia, Madrid, Barcelona, Bogotá, UNAM, and El Colegio de México.

Pei-jung Wu is a scholar of history, archaeology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at National Taiwan University and received her Ph.D. from UCLA in 2002 under Donald F. McCallum, also studying under Hironobu Kohara, Shou-chien Shih, and Yu-min Lee.

Pema Bhum is a Tibetologist who formerly served as a professor of Tibetan languages and letters at Lanzhou University and Indiana University Bloomington, and as director of the Latse Contemporary Tibetan Cultural Library (attested 2003–2009).

Pema Chödrön is a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Sarah Lawrence College and UC Berkeley. She studied under Chögyam Trungpa and other teachers, and served as director of Boulder Shambhala Center and as director and abbess of Gampo Abbey.
Pema Donyo Nyinje is active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Kalu Rinpoche and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and taught Ogyen Trinley Dorje and Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche.

Pema Gyaltsen is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang and Khenchen Palden Sherab Rinpoche, and taught Christopher S. George, Adam Pearcey, and Rizong Sras Rinpoche.
Pema Kunzang Tendzin studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.
Pema Sherpa is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar pursuing a Ph.D. in Religious Studies at McMaster University under the supervision of Shayne Clarke (attested 2026).
Pema Tekchok Loden studied under Shenphen Nangwa, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Shechen Gyaltsab, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.
Pema Tekchok Tenpai Gyeltsen studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and taught Shenphen Nangwa, Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang, and Shechen Gyaltsab.
Pema Tsering is a Tibetologist who studied under Shenphen Nangwa and served as an editorial consultant at the University of Bonn (attested 1982).
Pema Vajra 01 studied under Shenphen Nangwa, Patrul Rinpoche, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He taught Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Shechen Gyaltsab, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.
Pema Wangchok Gyelpo studied under Shenphen Nangwa, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Khakyab Dorje, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He taught Shenphen Nangwa and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.
